note.explanation: Stem cells are unspecialized cells. They can make new cells that differentiate into particular specialized cell types. Some stem cells remain in the body and help maintain or repair tissues.
examples: Skin stem cells help in wound healing.
Bone marrow stem cells differentiate to make different types of blood cells and immune cells.
note.checkAnswer: Stem cells are undifferentiated or unspecialized cells that can differentiate into specific cells.
note.simple: A stem cell is a cell that has not yet become a particular kind of cell. It can develop into specific cell types.

examTips: A short-answer question may ask you to define a stem cell. For full marks, include both that it is unspecialized or undifferentiated and that it can differentiate into specific cells.

You may be asked for examples of stem-cell roles. Link each example to its location: skin stem cells help in wound healing, liver stem cells help repair damage, and bone marrow stem cells make blood and immune cells.
Use the terms differentiate and specialized cells accurately; do not describe a stem cell as already being a particular specialized cell.

explain.title: What is a stem cell?
explain.body: Stem cells are undifferentiated or unspecialized cells that can differentiate into specific cells.

explain.title: Stem cells during development
explain.body: The earliest stem cell is the zygote. As it divides, it makes different cell lines, and cells in each line differentiate into types such as skin, muscle, nerve and blood cells.

explain.title: Stem cells in the body
explain.body: Stem cells remain in different parts of the body throughout life. They can divide and differentiate into specific cells as the body needs them.

explain.title: Repair and maintenance
explain.body: Under the right conditions, stem cells can regenerate damaged tissue. Skin stem cells help in wound healing, liver stem cells help repair liver damage, and bone marrow stem cells make blood and immune cells.

mistakes: Do not define a stem cell only as a cell that divides; include its ability to differentiate into specific cells.
Do not confuse stem cells with specialized cells such as nerve cells or red blood cells.
Do not say that all stem cells make the same cell type; their differentiation depends on the type of stem cell and the body's needs.
When giving an example, do not mix up the locations: bone marrow stem cells make blood and immune cells.
